claim: Cholesterol accounts for 23% of the total cholesterol in the body even though the brain represents only 2% of the total body weight.
source: The brain is the most cholesterol-rich organ, accounting for 23% of the total cholesterol in the body even though the brain represents only 2% of the total body weight (Dietschy and Turley, 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to Dietschy and Turley, 2004

claim: About 70–80% of the brain cholesterol resides in myelin.
source: About 70–80% of the brain cholesterol resides in myelin, a compact multilayer membrane structure that is generated by oligodendrocytes in the central nervous system (CNS), and myelin is critical for rapid saltatory nerve conduction (Armati and Mathey, 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Armati and Mathey, 2010

claim: Cholesterol accounts for the highest molar percentage (~52%) among all myelin lipids.
source: Myelin is a lipid-rich material, and cholesterol accounts for the highest molar percentage (~52%) among all myelin lipids (Chrast et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chrast et al., 2011

claim: The rate of cholesterol biosynthesis in the mouse brain is highest during the first three weeks after birth.
source: Consistently, the rate of cholesterol biosynthesis in the mouse brain is highest during the first three weeks after birth (Dietschy and Turley, 2004; Quan et al., 2003), the same period in which the rate of myelinogenesis is highest (Armati and Mathey, 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to Dietschy and Turley, 2004 and Quan et al., 2003

claim: The blood-brain barrier blocks the uptake of cholesterol from the circulation.
source: The brain depends extensively on de novo cholesterol biosynthesis, which is mainly carried out by oligodendrocytes and astrocytes, as the blood-brain barrier blocks the uptake of cholesterol from the circulation (Camargo et al., 2017; Saher et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citations to Camargo et al., 2017 and Saher et al., 2005

claim: Genetic ablation of squalene synthase (Fdft1) in oligodendrocyte lineage cells results in failure of proper myelination.
source: Genetic ablation of squalene synthase (Fdft1), an enzyme involved in the early step of cholesterol biosynthesis, in oligodendrocyte lineage cells has resulted in failure of proper myelination (Saher et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to Saher et al., 2005

claim: Smith–Lemli–Opitz syndrome (SLOS) is caused by mutations of the cholesterol biosynthesis gene encoding 7-dehydrocholesterol reductase (DHCR7).
source: For example, hereditary diseases such as Smith–Lemli–Opitz syndrome (SLOS), desmosterolosis, and lathosterolosis are caused by mutations of the cholesterol biosynthesis genes encoding 7-dehydrocholesterol reductase (DHCR7), 24-dehydrocholesterol reductase (DHCR24), and sterol-C5-desaturase (SC5D), respectively (Kanungo et al., 2013; Nwokoro et al., 2001; Porter and Herman, 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kanungo et al., 2013; Nwokoro et al., 2001; Porter and Herman, 2011

claim: SLOS patients present with cognitive defects and delayed motor and language development along with hypomyelination.
source: In particular, SLOS patients present with cognitive defects and delayed motor and language development along with hypomyelination (Porter and Herman, 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Porter and Herman, 2011

claim: Patients with desmosterolosis have defects in the corpus callosum, thinning of white matter, and seizures.
source: Patients with desmosterolosis have defects in the corpus callosum, thinning of white matter, and seizures (Zerenturk et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zerenturk et al., 2013

claim: One of the 108 schizophrenia-associated genomic loci is on chromosome 22q13.2, which includes SREBF2 gene that encodes sterol regulatory element-binding protein 2 (SREBP2).
source: Of note, among the 108 schizophrenia-associated genomic loci, one is on chromosome 22q13.2, which includes SREBF2 gene that encodes sterol regulatory element-binding protein 2 (SREBP2), the major transcription factor that regulates cholesterol biosynthesis (Horton et al., 2002; Le Hellard et al., 2010; Steen et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Horton et al., 2002; Le Hellard et al., 2010; Steen et al., 2017

claim: Antipsychotic drugs increase SREBP2 activity, resulting in upregulated expression of the genes involved in cholesterol biosynthesis.
source: Antipsychotic drugs are known to increase SREBP2 activity, resulting in upregulated expression of the genes involved in cholesterol biosynthesis (Fernø et al., 2005; Le Hellard et al., 2009), suggesting a potential role of SREBP2-mediated cholesterol biosynthesis in the pathogenesis of schizophrenia.
evidence: Supported by citations to Fernø et al., 2005; Le Hellard et al., 2009

claim: Mammalian Quaking (Qk) undergoes alternative splicing to express the RNA-binding proteins Qki-5, Qki-6, and Qki-7.
source: Mammalian Quaking (Qk) undergoes alternative splicing to express the RNA-binding proteins Qki-5, Qki-6, and Qki-7 (Darbelli and Richard, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Darbelli and Richard, 2016

claim: Qki regulates the RNA processing of the genes encoding myelin basic protein (MBP), myelin-associated glycoprotein (MAG), p27kip1, and neurofascin 155 in oligodendrocytes.
source: Various studies have extensively demonstrated that Qki regulates the RNA processing of the genes encoding myelin basic protein (MBP), myelin-associated glycoprotein (MAG), p27kip1, and neurofascin 155 in oligodendrocytes (Darbelli et al., 2016; Larocque et al., 2005; Larocque et al., 2002; Li et al., 2000; Zhao et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to Darbelli et al., 2016; Larocque et al., 2005; Larocque et al., 2002; Li et al., 2000; Zhao et al., 2010

claim: The quaking viable (qkv) mouse is a spontaneous recessive mutant with an approximate 1-Mbp deletion in the upstream of Qk locus, leading to diminished expression of Qki in oligodendrocytes.
source: The quaking viable (qkv) mouse is a spontaneous recessive mutant with an approximate 1-Mbp deletion in the upstream of Qk locus, leading to diminished expression of Qki in oligodendrocytes (Ebersole et al., 1996; Hardy et al., 1996).
evidence: Supported by citations to Ebersole et al., 1996; Hardy et al., 1996

claim: Qkv homozygotes suffer from tremor and early death due to severe hypomyelination in the CNS.
source: Qkv homozygotes suffer from tremor and early death due to severe hypomyelination in the CNS (Sidman et al., 1964).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sidman et al., 1964

claim: qkv mice exhibited reduced myelin lipid content, including cholesterol.
source: Previous studies showed that qkv mice exhibited reduced myelin lipid content, including cholesterol (Baumann et al., 1968; Singh et al., 1971), and this phenomenon was thought to be secondary to impaired differentiation and maturation of oligodendrocytes (Chen et al., 2007; Darbelli et al., 2016; Larocque et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citations to Baumann et al., 1968; Singh et al., 1971

claim: Similar numbers of oligodendrocytes in some regions of the CNS in qkv mice and control mice and even hyperplasia in these regions in the former mice were observed.
source: However, similar numbers of oligodendrocytes in some regions of the CNS in qkv mice and control mice and even hyperplasia in these regions in the former mice were observed (Doukhanine et al., 2010; Hardy et al., 1996; Myers et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Doukhanine et al., 2010; Hardy et al., 1996; Myers et al., 2016

claim: Qki is not required for mature oligodendrocyte survival in adult mice.
source: Interestingly, our recent study demonstrated that Qki is not required for mature oligodendrocyte survival in adult mice, and that Qki-5 forms a complex with peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor beta (PPARβ)-retinoid X receptor alpha (RXRα) to transcriptionally control fatty acid metabolism, which is essential for mature myelin maintenance (Zhou et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhou et al., 2020

claim: Qki-5 forms a complex with peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor beta (PPARβ)-retinoid X receptor alpha (RXRα) to transcriptionally control fatty acid metabolism, which is essential for mature myelin maintenance.
source: Interestingly, our recent study demonstrated that Qki is not required for mature oligodendrocyte survival in adult mice, and that Qki-5 forms a complex with peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor beta (PPARβ)-retinoid X receptor alpha (RXRα) to transcriptionally control fatty acid metabolism, which is essential for mature myelin maintenance (Zhou et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhou et al., 2020

claim: Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice began to exhibit visible tremors and ataxia about 12 days after tamoxifen injection.
source: About 12 days after tamoxifen injection, Nestin-CreERT2;QkL/L mice (hereafter denoted as 'Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice') began to exhibit visible tremors and ataxia accompanied by a significant reduction in coordinate movement as measured using the rotarod test and a marked growth retardation (Figure 1B–D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, Video 1).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice had a median survival duration of 13 days after tamoxifen injection.
source: Neurological deficits in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice progressed quite rapidly, and the mice eventually displayed hunched posture, paralysis, and hyperpnea, with a median survival duration of 13 days after tamoxifen injection (Figure 1E).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice had severe hypomyelination as evidenced by substantial reduction in the levels of expression of MBP, proteolipid protein (PLP), and MAG (23.7%, 28.2%, and 16.6% of those in control mice, respectively).
source: Two weeks after tamoxifen injection (in all subsequent experiments unless specified otherwise), Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice had severe hypomyelination as evidenced by substantial reduction in the levels of expression of MBP, proteolipid protein (PLP), and MAG (23.7%, 28.2%, and 16.6% of those in control mice, respectively) and a marked increase in the frequency (4.1-fold greater than that in control mice) of Iba1+ microglial infiltration in the corpus callosum tissues (Figure 1F).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice had a marked increase in the frequency (4.1-fold greater than that in control mice) of Iba1+ microglial infiltration in the corpus callosum tissues.
source: Two weeks after tamoxifen injection (in all subsequent experiments unless specified otherwise), Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice had severe hypomyelination as evidenced by substantial reduction in the levels of expression of MBP, proteolipid protein (PLP), and MAG (23.7%, 28.2%, and 16.6% of those in control mice, respectively) and a marked increase in the frequency (4.1-fold greater than that in control mice) of Iba1+ microglial infiltration in the corpus callosum tissues (Figure 1F).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: The percentage of the GFP+ area in the corpus callosum tissues in Qk-Nestin-iCKO;mTmG mice markedly decreased relative to that in control Nestin-CreERT2;mTmG mice (10.6% vs. 68.7%).
source: The percentage of the GFP+ area in the corpus callosum tissues in Qk-Nestin-iCKO;mTmG mice markedly decreased relative to that in control Nestin-CreERT2;mTmG mice (10.6% vs. 68.7%; Figure 1F).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: Only 23.3% of the axons were myelinated in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice, whereas compact myelin formed in 79.0% of the axons in control mice.
source: In line with these findings, ultrastructural analyses of myelin sheaths in the optic nerves using transmission electron microscopy revealed that only 23.3% of the axons were myelinated in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice, whereas compact myelin formed in 79.0% of the axons in control mice (Figure 1H, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study using transmission electron microscopy

claim: The myelin sheaths wrapping the sparse axons in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice were considerably thinner than those in control mice and failed to form the compact myelin structure (g-ratio, 0.94 vs. 0.78; p<0.0001).
source: The myelin sheaths wrapping the sparse axons in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice were considerably thinner than those in control mice and failed to form the compact myelin structure (g-ratio, 0.94 vs. 0.78; p<0.0001; Figure 1H).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study with statistical analysis

claim: Qki depletion slowed down the myelin formation during P12–P21, a time frame in which myelin is initiated and actively generated.
source: We further performed a time-course analysis of MBP expression in the corpus callosum to compare the efficiency of myelin formation between Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice and control mice during the critical time of myelin growth (P12–P21). Qki depletion slowed down the myelin formation during P12–P21, a time frame in which myelin is initiated and actively generated, ultimately resulting in failure of proper myelin formation at P21 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: Qki depletion leads to defect in formation of node of Ranvier at P21 in the optic nerve.
source: Notably, we observed that Qki depletion leads to defect in formation of node of Ranvier at P21 in the optic nerve, where rapid and robust myelination occurs during development, using antibodies against paranodal protein (Caspr) and nodal proteins (AnkG and PanNav) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: Defect in node formation was observed as early as P14, which cannot be overcome at P21.
source: Defect in node formation was observed as early as P14, which cannot be overcome at P21 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E, F), and this observation is in line with the defect in myelination observed from P12 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: Total number of nodes (including both intact and the incomplete nodes) in the optic nerve was decreased upon Qki depletion.
source: Specifically, total number of nodes (including both intact and the incomplete nodes) in the optic nerve was decreased upon Qki depletion (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: The percentage of intact nodes among the total nodes was significantly reduced with Qki depletion.
source: Importantly, the percentage of intact nodes among the total nodes was significantly reduced with Qki depletion (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: The axonal diameter and density of axon in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice were comparable with those in control mice.
source: Despite severely compromised axonal ensheathment and defective structure of node of Ranvier, the axonal diameter and density of axon in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice were comparable with those in control mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1I, J), and no evidence of axonal damage was detected in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice via immunofluorescent staining of amyloid precursor protein (Figure 1I).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: No evidence of axonal damage was detected in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice via immunofluorescent staining of amyloid precursor protein.
source: Despite severely compromised axonal ensheathment and defective structure of node of Ranvier, the axonal diameter and density of axon in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice were comparable with those in control mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1I, J), and no evidence of axonal damage was detected in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice via immunofluorescent staining of amyloid precursor protein (Figure 1I).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: The length of AIS labeled by AnkG at the proximal axon adjacent to the soma (NeuN) was not altered in the cortex region of Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice compared to control mice.
source: In addition, we further asked if Qki loss impacts on the axon initial segment (AIS) structure. We found that the length of AIS labeled by AnkG at the proximal axon adjacent to the soma (NeuN) was not altered in the cortex region of Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice compared to control mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1K–M), further suggesting that the integrity of the axon was not affected upon Qki depletion.
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: Depletion of Qki in mouse NSCs results in severe neurological deficits due to hypomyelination in the CNS accompanied by the defect in node formation.
source: Taken together, these data demonstrated that depletion of Qki in mouse NSCs results in severe neurological deficits due to hypomyelination in the CNS accompanied by the defect in node formation.
evidence: Inference from experimental observations in the study

claim: The number of Pdgfrα+ OPCs in the developing cortex tissues in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice was slightly higher than that in control mice.
source: Excluding the first possibility, we found that the number of Pdgfrα+ OPCs in the developing cortex tissues in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice was slightly higher than that in control mice (Figure 2A), probably due to a compensatory increase in the proliferation of OPCs in response to hypomyelination.
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: 92.6% of Pdgfrα+ OPCs in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice lacked expression of Qki.
source: Notably, 92.6% of Pdgfrα+ OPCs in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice lacked expression of Qki, indicating that Qki does not affect the generation or survival of OPCs.
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: The numbers of Aspa+ and Gstpi+ mature oligodendrocytes in the corpus callosum tissues in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice were comparable to those in control mice.
source: Excluding the second possibility above, immunofluorescent staining of Aspa and Gstpi, two well-established markers of mature oligodendrocytes, revealed that the numbers of Aspa+ and Gstpi+ mature oligodendrocytes in the corpus callosum tissues in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice were comparable to those in control mice (Figure 2B, C).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: The majority of Aspa+ and Gstpi+ oligodendrocytes in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice lacked expression of Qki.
source: The majority of these Aspa+ and Gstpi+ oligodendrocytes in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice lacked expression of Qki (Figure 2B, C), indicating that OPCs without expression of Qki are still capable of differentiating into Aspa+Gstpi+ mature oligodendrocytes.
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: OPCs without expression of Qki are still capable of differentiating into Aspa+Gstpi+ mature oligodendrocytes.
source: The majority of these Aspa+ and Gstpi+ oligodendrocytes in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice lacked expression of Qki (Figure 2B, C), indicating that OPCs without expression of Qki are still capable of differentiating into Aspa+Gstpi+ mature oligodendrocytes.
evidence: Inference from experimental observation in the study

claim: The CC-1 antibody actually recognizes Qki-7.
source: Of note, we did not use another commonly used marker, CC-1, in our study because a recent study demonstrated that the CC-1 antibody actually recognizes Qki-7 (Bin et al., 2016), raising the concern that CC-1 is not a good marker for labeling mature oligodendrocyte in Qk-knockout mice.
evidence: Supported by citation to Bin et al., 2016

claim: The number of CC-1+ mature oligodendrocytes in the corpus callosum tissues in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice significantly decreased to 6.7% of that in control mice.
source: In fact, the number of CC-1+ mature oligodendrocytes in the corpus callosum tissues in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice significantly decreased to 6.7% of that in control mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), whereas the number of Aspa+Gstpi+ oligodendrocytes in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice was similar to that in control mice.
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: The Aspa+Gstpi+ oligodendrocytes in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice cannot be recognized by CC-1 antibodies due to the absence of Qki-7 in these cells.
source: The reason for this phenomenon is that the Aspa+Gstpi+ oligodendrocytes in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice cannot be recognized by CC-1 antibodies due to the absence of Qki-7 in these cells.
evidence: Inference from experimental observations in the study

claim: Aspa and Gstpi positivities represented the same mature oligodendrocyte population.
source: Also, co-immunofluorescent staining of Aspa and Gstpi demonstrated that they represent the same mature oligodendrocyte population (Figure 2D).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: The mRNA level of Aspa in myelinating oligodendrocytes was much higher than that in newly formed oligodendrocytes and OPCs.
source: Analyses of the previous transcriptomic studies (Marques et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2014) revealed that the mRNA level of Aspa in myelinating oligodendrocytes was much higher than that in newly formed oligodendrocytes and OPCs (Figure 2E, F).
evidence: Analysis of previous transcriptomic studies cited

claim: Aspa+Gstpi+ mature oligodendrocytes represent a subset of myelin-forming oligodendrocytes.
source: Coupled with the observation that Aspa and Gstpi positivities represented the same mature oligodendrocyte population (Figure 2D), these data demonstrated that Aspa+Gstpi+ mature oligodendrocytes represent a subset of myelin-forming oligodendrocytes.
evidence: Inference from experimental observations in the study

claim: The number of Olig2+ cells in the corpus callosum tissues in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice was 50.9% lower than that in control mice.
source: Of note, the number of Olig2+ (marker of oligodendroglial lineage) cells in the corpus callosum tissues in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice was 50.9% lower than that in control mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that Qki loss partially blocks OPCs differentiation into Olig2+Aspa-Gstpi- oligodendroglial lineage cells.
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: Qki loss partially blocks OPCs differentiation into Olig2+Aspa-Gstpi- oligodendroglial lineage cells.
source: Of note, the number of Olig2+ (marker of oligodendroglial lineage) cells in the corpus callosum tissues in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice was 50.9% lower than that in control mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that Qki loss partially blocks OPCs differentiation into Olig2+Aspa-Gstpi- oligodendroglial lineage cells.
evidence: Inference from experimental observation in the study

claim: Numbers of TUNEL positive cells were comparable between Qk-Nestin-iCKO and control.
source: Still, numbers of TUNEL positive cells were comparable between Qk-Nestin-iCKO and control (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that the survival of oligodendroglial lineage cells was not affected upon Qki depletion.
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: The survival of oligodendroglial lineage cells was not affected upon Qki depletion.
source: Still, numbers of TUNEL positive cells were comparable between Qk-Nestin-iCKO and control (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that the survival of oligodendroglial lineage cells was not affected upon Qki depletion.
evidence: Inference from experimental observation in the study

claim: NSCs without expression of Qki are still capable of generating OPCs and subsequently differentiating into Aspa+Gstpi+ myelinating oligodendrocytes.
source: Taken together, these data suggested that NSCs without expression of Qki are still capable of generating OPCs and subsequently differentiating into Aspa+Gstpi+ myelinating oligodendrocytes.
evidence: Inference from experimental observations in the study

claim: Comparable numbers of neurons were found in the brains in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice and control mice.
source: Immunofluorescent staining of NeuN (a marker of neurons) revealed comparable numbers of neurons in the brains in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice and control mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: Sox9+Gfap+GFP+ astrocytes only constituted a small population among total Sox9+Gfap+ astrocytes in both Qk-Nestin-iCKO;mTmG mice (15.92%) and control Nestin-CreERT2;mTmG mice (16.22%).
source: Notably, Sox9+Gfap+GFP+ astrocytes only constituted a small population among total Sox9+Gfap+ astrocytes in both Qk-Nestin-iCKO;mTmG mice (15.92%) and control Nestin-CreERT2;mTmG mice (16.22%) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B), suggesting that the majority of Sox9+Gfap+ astrocytes are developed prior to P7 and therefore are not targeted by Nestin-CreERT2 inducible system with P7 tamoxifen treatment.
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: The majority of Sox9+Gfap+ astrocytes are developed prior to P7 and therefore are not targeted by Nestin-CreERT2 inducible system with P7 tamoxifen treatment.
source: Notably, Sox9+Gfap+GFP+ astrocytes only constituted a small population among total Sox9+Gfap+ astrocytes in both Qk-Nestin-iCKO;mTmG mice (15.92%) and control Nestin-CreERT2;mTmG mice (16.22%) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B), suggesting that the majority of Sox9+Gfap+ astrocytes are developed prior to P7 and therefore are not targeted by Nestin-CreERT2 inducible system with P7 tamoxifen treatment.
evidence: Inference from experimental observation in the study

claim: Qki loss in NSCs has minimal or no effect on the neuron and astrocyte populations in the brain.
source: Collectively, these data suggested that Qki loss in NSCs has minimal or no effect on the neuron and astrocyte populations in the brain, and hypomyelination induced by Qki loss is not secondary to defects in neurons or astrocytes.
evidence: Inference from experimental observations in the study

claim: Hypomyelination induced by Qki loss is not secondary to defects in neurons or astrocytes.
source: Collectively, these data suggested that Qki loss in NSCs has minimal or no effect on the neuron and astrocyte populations in the brain, and hypomyelination induced by Qki loss is not secondary to defects in neurons or astrocytes.
evidence: Inference from experimental observations in the study

claim: Expression of MBP in the corpus callosum tissues was greatly reduced upon Qki depletion.
source: Consistent with previous studies demonstrating that Qki regulates the RNA homeostasis of myelin proteins, including MBP (Darbelli et al., 2016; Larocque et al., 2005; Larocque et al., 2002; Li et al., 2000; Zhao et al., 2010), we found that expression of MBP in the corpus callosum tissues was greatly reduced upon Qki depletion.
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: An uneven and patchy MBP staining pattern was detected in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice.
source: In addition, unlike the homogeneous MBP staining in control mice, an uneven and patchy MBP staining pattern was detected in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice (Figure 3A), implicating that MBP was not properly assembled in myelin sheaths other than a reduction in its expression.
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: MBP was not properly assembled in myelin sheaths in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice other than a reduction in its expression.
source: In addition, unlike the homogeneous MBP staining in control mice, an uneven and patchy MBP staining pattern was detected in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice (Figure 3A), implicating that MBP was not properly assembled in myelin sheaths other than a reduction in its expression.
evidence: Inference from experimental observation in the study

claim: The MBP and PLP co-localization rate markedly decreased in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice (45.7% vs. 88.5%).
source: We also found that whereas MBP and PLP co-localized very well in the corpus callosum tissues in control mice, the MBP and PLP co-localization rate markedly decreased in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice (45.7% vs. 88.5%; Figure 3B).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: The MBP and MAG co-localization rate in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice was substantially lower than that in control mice (26.9% vs. 75.1%).
source: Similarly, the MBP and MAG co-localization rate in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice was substantially lower than that in control mice (26.9% vs. 75.1%; Figure 3C).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: The proper interaction of myelin proteins such as PLP, MBP, and MAG with myelin lipids is required for formation of raft-like domains on myelin membrane, which is essential for myelin membrane assembly.
source: Previous studies demonstrated that the proper interaction of myelin proteins such as PLP, MBP, and MAG with myelin lipids is required for formation of raft-like domains on myelin membrane, which is essential for myelin membrane assembly (Aggarwal et al., 2011; Ozgen et al., 2016; Saher et al., 2005; Simons et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citations to Aggarwal et al., 2011; Ozgen et al., 2016; Saher et al., 2005; Simons et al., 2000

claim: The percentage of the FluoroMyelin+ area was 88.7% in control mice but only 6.6% in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice.
source: The percentage of the FluoroMyelin+ area was 88.7% in control mice but only 6.6% in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice (Figure 3D).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: The ratio of FluoroMyelin to PLP in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice was only about one fourth of that in control mice.
source: More importantly, although the levels of both PLP and FluoroMyelin in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice were lower than those in control mice, the ratio of FluoroMyelin to PLP in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice was only about one fourth of that in control mice (Figure 3E), suggesting that the levels of myelin lipids were more profoundly reduced than were the levels of myelin proteins upon Qki depletion (Figure 1F, Figure 3D).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: The levels of myelin lipids were more profoundly reduced than were the levels of myelin proteins upon Qki depletion.
source: More importantly, although the levels of both PLP and FluoroMyelin in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice were lower than those in control mice, the ratio of FluoroMyelin to PLP in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice was only about one fourth of that in control mice (Figure 3E), suggesting that the levels of myelin lipids were more profoundly reduced than were the levels of myelin proteins upon Qki depletion (Figure 1F, Figure 3D).
evidence: Inference from experimental observation in the study

claim: The expression of Gstpi was strongly upregulated in the corpus callosum tissues of Qk-NSC-iCKO mice.
source: Of note, the expression of Gstpi was strongly upregulated in the corpus callosum tissues of Qk-NSC-iCKO mice (Figure 2C).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study

claim: Aspa+Gstpi+ mature oligodendrocytes in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice might cope with imbalanced ratio of myelin lipids to myelin proteins by elevating Gstpi.
source: Since Gstpi has been implicated in stress response (Bartolini and Galli, 2016), we reasoned that Aspa+Gstpi+ mature oligodendrocytes in Qk-Nestin-iCKO mice might cope with imbalanced ratio of myelin lipids to myelin proteins by elevating Gstpi.
evidence: Inference from experimental observation and cited knowledge

claim: The myelin lipid components are disrupted by Qki loss in oligodendrocytes, which may consequently lead to defective assembly of myelin proteins with myelin lipids and inability to form compact myelin.
source: Taken together, these data suggested that the myelin lipid components are disrupted by Qki loss in oligodendrocytes, which may consequently lead to defective assembly of myelin proteins with myelin lipids and inability to form compact myelin.

claim: All Qk-Plp-iCKO mice began to experience tremors and ataxia about 11 days after tamoxifen injection.

claim: Long-term benefits of cholesterol supplementation have not been clearly examined.
source: However, challenges still remain, as cholesterol rarely crosses the blood-brain barrier, and long-term benefits of cholesterol supplementation have not been clearly examined (Tierney et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Tierney et al., 2010

claim: Qki plays an important role in intracellular vesicle trafficking in NSCs.
source: Of note, we previously demonstrated that Qki plays an important role in intracellular vesicle trafficking in NSCs (Shingu et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Shingu et al., 2017

claim: If the same function of Qki exists in oligodendrocytes, cholesterol transport and uptake would be impaired due to defective intracellular vesicle trafficking in Qki-depleted oligodendrocytes.
source: If the same function of Qki exists in oligodendrocytes, cholesterol transport and uptake would be impaired due to defective intracellular vesicle trafficking in Qki-depleted oligodendrocytes, which may lead to inefficiencies in high-cholesterol diet-based therapy.
evidence: Speculation based on previous observation

claim: QKI is one of the genes most associated with various neurological diseases.
source: As QKI is one of the genes most associated with various neurological diseases (Darbelli and Richard, 2016), understanding the mechanisms underpinning Qki/Srebp2-mediated cholesterol biosynthesis and myelination will help identify tissue-specific therapeutic opportunities for neurological diseases associated with myelin defects (Nwokoro et al., 2001; Porter and Herman, 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Darbelli and Richard, 2016
